items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: I mean we were playing like a Kurt Weill’s tune, a Kurt Weill’s tune today at the jazz camp and I was trying to find a different harmonization on “Mack the Knife,” you know that will keep it fresh than what people would play.

ctx.x: I guess that’s the magic of it, those moments when people find things that didn’t work before and make something out of it.

Oh yeah and that happens a lot. I mean I’m still discovering things. I mean we were playing like a Kurt Weill’s tune, a Kurt Weill’s tune today at the jazz camp and I was trying to find a different harmonization on “Mack the Knife,” you know that will keep it fresh than what people would play. I mean you could take even very simple things and find from your analysis well this is what we’ll do differently to reharmonize this and still make it beautiful but make it subtle so that when people hear it, they won’t…
I brought a little example of you here.
